title: ContextVariation
description: A named test-design condition, classified by test type (functional, load, security, regression, smoke, exploratory), under which a TestCoverageTarget is to be exercised, optionally bound to a set of EnvironmentFactors that fix the concrete environment for that condition. It names the whole execution context. It does not name a single environmental variable or an input value. Use EnvironmentFactor instead when the element is a single concrete environmental variable and its value (e.g. 'Ubuntu 22.04', 'en-US', 'latency < 100ms'), not a named test context that groups such variables. Use CoverageRequirement instead when the element states coverage criteria (pairwise, boundary-values, MC/DC) that must be met, possibly across several contexts, rather than defining one context. Use InputSpacePartition instead when the variation is in the data fed to the target (an input field's equivalence classes), not in the type of test or the execution environment. Use OutcomeCategory instead when the element classifies the expected result (success, timeout, validation-error), not the conditions under which the test runs.

description.description: Free-text explanation of the execution condition this variation represents: its purpose, scope and how it differs from other contexts applied to the same target, such as 'peak-load run at 500 rps against staging'. Set it whenever the contextType alone does not identify the context uniquely.

contextType.description: The category of test context this variation represents

environmentFactors.description: References EnvironmentFactor nodes specifying the concrete environmental constraints (OS, locale, network, hardware, dependency versions) that define this context variation.

x-dr-standard: IEEE 829-2008 Test Design Specification – Approach refinements and Environmental needs (Clause 9 Level Test Plan: environmental needs)
x-dr-evidence: Separate test suites or directories split by test type, such as tests/load, tests/security, tests/smoke, or pytest markers / JUnit @Tag('smoke'|'regression') used to select runs
CI pipeline jobs or matrix entries that run the same targets under named contexts, e.g. a 'load' job invoking k6/JMeter or a 'security' job invoking OWASP ZAP, each with its own environment variables

Test configuration profiles bundling environment settings per context, e.g. playwright.config projects, tox envs, or application-test-load.yml, that set OS, locale, network throttling or dependency versions
